newsitem.title: FRANCE: France not to recoup textile aid despite EU ban.
newsitem.headline: France not to recoup textile aid despite EU ban.

text.p: French Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Wednesday that the government would not ask textile and clothing companies to pay back benefits accorded under a French state aid scheme, despite an EU ban.

His statement at a news conference came after the European Commission said on Wednesday it had banned the French aid plan that involves cuts or exemptions in social security contributions for low-paid workers.
Borotra estimated the amount for the 500 companies and 110,000 employees so far involved was 500 million francs.
"It is not in my eyes plausible to ask for a reimbursement of the reduction in charges," Borotra said.
He said the measure had already been passed by parliament and only "the law can undo what the law has done" and the state was committed to a "contractual process" with the companies.
In addition, he said, such a move would "be catastrophic...as it would destroy jobs."
The commission said on Wednesday that it was open to discussion to extend the existing subsidies to other sectors that are heavily dependent on manual labour.
Borotra said talks were continuing with the Commission on a widening of the plan.
He added that the government was currently in interministerial talks to work out how the plan could be extended given budgetary restraints.
The French plan has been allocated a budget of around 2.1 billion for the first year and is due to run 18 months.
The Commission said the French plan did not create problems for some 11,300 of the 13,000 firms concerned since the benefits they received did not exceed minimum thresholds for state aid.
"On the other hand, the Commission's decision requires the aid to be recovered in cases where that threshold is exceeded," the Commissions aid.
The textile plan began in June 1996.
